items.item_text: California Clinical Laboratory Scientist License.
Must be able to work various hours and locations based on business needs.
Employment is subject to a criminal background check and a pre-employment physical.
Bachelor's Degree in business or healthcare administration or related area; and/or equivalent combination of experience/training.
Master’s degree in healthcare administration, business administration, or related fields.
A minimum of seven (7) or more years of relevant experience.
Experience in a large hospital, academic medical center, or integrated health system.
Experience and proven success in technical proficiency in laboratory techniques and procedures.
Experience in laboratory testing with an emphasis on Chemistry, Hematology, Coagulation & Blood Bank.
Experience with laboratory automation, LIS, instrumentation implementation, validation, and process improvement.
Experience with regulatory agencies, such as FDA, AAB, & CAP.
Lean, Six Sigma, or other process improvement experience.

Provides daily operational management support for the Clinical Laboratory in assigned areas. Manages productivity, technical performance of specimen processing and laboratory testing and efficient operations of equipment.

The Manager works collaboratively with laboratory leadership, medical directors, supervisors, staff and clinical partners to translate organizational priorities to effective daily operations and improvements.
Direct daily laboratory operations, including staffing, productivity, quality, and service delivery.
Develop and implement operational strategies to support organizational priorities and laboratory goals.
Provide leadership during staffing shortages, system interruptions, high-volume periods, and other operational challenges.
Identify opportunities to improve laboratory processes, workflows, and overall operational effectiveness.
Regulatory Compliance & Inspection Readiness
Ensure compliance with CLIA, CAP, CDPH, safety requirements, and organizational policies and procedures.
Maintain continuous inspection readiness and ensure laboratory operations meet applicable regulatory and accreditation standards.
Oversee appropriate investigation, documentation, and corrective action related to quality, compliance, and operational issues.
Team Leadership & Development
Lead, develop, and support supervisors and laboratory staff.
Participate in recruitment, performance management, employee development, and succession planning.
Foster a collaborative, accountable, and service-focused team environment.
Support staff engagement, professional growth, and effective performance management.
Quality & Performance Management
Monitor key performance indicators, including turnaround times, quality, productivity, staffing, and service metrics.
Use operational and quality data to guide decision-making, identify trends, and drive continuous improvement.
Monitor laboratory performance and implement corrective actions when performance or quality goals are not met.
Promote a culture of quality, safety, accountability, and continuous improvement. Process Improvement & Innovation
Lead initiatives to improve laboratory processes, workflows, efficiency, and service delivery.
Lead the implementation and integration of new instrumentation, automation, testing methodologies, information systems, and operational processes.
Evaluate the impact of new technologies and processes on quality, productivity, staffing, and patient care.
Financial & Resource Management
Participate in budget management, staffing plans, equipment selection, and resource allocation.
Optimize staffing and laboratory resources to support operational needs, productivity, quality, and financial goals.
Evaluate operational needs and support decisions regarding equipment, technology, and other laboratory resources.
Clinical & Interdisciplinary Collaboration
Collaborate with physicians, nursing, laboratory medical and technical leadership, and other departments to resolve issues and improve patient care.
Partner with interdisciplinary leaders to support effective communication, coordination, and integration of laboratory services.
Serve as a laboratory leadership resource during complex operational and patient-care situations.
While not required, a cover letter is highly recommended when applying to this position.
Demonstrated knowledge of management theory, economic impact and management functions.
Proven ability to apply technical knowledge and skills to improve operations and management.
